one_liner: Team lead managing USPTO office space, renovation and move projects in Alexandria, coordinating with GSA, contractors and office directors, and overseeing contractor funding and invoices.
fit_summary: This GS-14 role requires one full year of GS-13-equivalent experience managing space, construction or renovation projects, overseeing alteration funding and contractor invoices as a COR or similar, and leading a team. Daniel's emergency-management consulting at IEM and strengths in policy and relationships do not clearly match facilities and space project management. Unless Daniel's IEM work included senior facilities, construction or contract-oversight duties, Daniel is unlikely to qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public and federal transition (fed-transition) applicants, so Daniel can apply without federal status.

Requires one full year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to GS-13, covering space/construction project management, space planning, project funding and COR-type contractor oversight, and team leadership.
Education cannot substitute for experience at this grade.
Security clearance is listed as 'Other'; expect a background investigation, and confirm details in the full announcement.
All qualifications must be met by the closing date, October 30, 2026.
strategy: Before applying, honestly compare your IEM duties with each of the four specialized-experience areas. If you can't document a year at a GS-13-equivalent level in all of them, put your effort into better-matched postings.

If your IEM work included facility, site or space setup (for example, disaster recovery centers or field offices), contractor oversight, budgets, or leading staff, describe it in the posting's exact terms with dates and hours per week.
Preview the questionnaire at the provided link before writing your resume. Answer it truthfully, because the posting warns that overstating qualifications can get you removed from consideration.
Keep the resume to two pages. Spell out each specialized-experience element briefly and give concrete project sizes, budgets and numbers of stakeholders.

Use this posting's requirements as a benchmark, and consider GS-11/12 emergency management, program analyst (0301) or intergovernmental/public affairs roles that better match your consulting and people skills.
The application window is short (October 20–30, 2026), so prepare documents in advance and submit well before the deadline.
resume_bullets: Managed [number] [type of facility/site/office] projects valued at [$ amount] from initiation through completion, tracking schedules, milestones, deliverables and budgets for [client agency].
Reviewed contractor deliverables, reports and invoices for [contract/task order] totaling [$ amount], verifying work against scopes of work in a role comparable to a COR.
Served as team lead for [number] staff, assigning and balancing work, reviewing products for accuracy, and briefing [manager/client] on workload issues and project risks.
interview_questions: Describe a renovation or space project you managed from initiation through completion. How did you keep it within scope, schedule and budget?
How have you resolved a disagreement between an office director and a space planner or GSA over a layout or space allocation?
Walk us through how you verify contractor work and invoices before approving payment.
How do you assign and balance work across a team while managing several projects at once?
watch_outs: The specialized experience is narrow (facilities, space planning, COR oversight), and your background as known does not show it.
The application window is only 10 days, closing October 30, 2026.
The role is on-site in Alexandria, with only 52 hours of telework per leave year, which matters for the commute from Manassas.
The questionnaire uses gold/silver/bronze categories, and inflated answers are grounds for removal.
